title: Plant Foundations
summary: Build a whole-plant mental model by moving from seed structure through roots, stems, nodes, leaves, flowers, and trichomes.
outcome: Identify the major plant structures and explain how each fits into the cannabis plant as a connected biological system.

title: Water & Transport
summary: Follow water from the root surface through vascular transport and leaf water loss, then connect that flow to atmospheric and root-zone demand.
outcome: Explain how root absorption, xylem flow, stomata, transpiration, VPD, and root-zone conditions interact.

title: Diagnostic Reasoning
summary: Learn an observation-first workflow that moves from a healthy baseline to symptom description, measurement context, and a ranked differential.
outcome: Describe plant symptoms precisely and choose measurements that separate plausible causes instead of diagnosing from appearance alone.

title: Canopy Architecture
summary: Connect nodes, apical dominance, training responses, light distribution, and airflow to understand how canopy structure develops.
outcome: Predict how branch orientation and training alter growing-point distribution, light exposure, and air exchange.

title: Reproduction & Breeding Biology
summary: Follow reproductive development from preflower identification through pollen movement, pollination response, seed formation, and controlled crosses.
outcome: Identify reproductive structures and explain the biological sequence from pollen production through seed development.

title: Flower & Trichome Observation
summary: Track flower development and learn a repeatable microscope workflow that treats trichome appearance as one maturity observation among several.
outcome: Inspect representative floral tissue consistently and combine flower development, trichome observations, and risk inspection without overclaiming chemistry.
